pulls.title: 8397415: Splash JPEG decoder may retain freed frame storage after an allocation failure
pulls.author: Sovtouch
pulls.body_excerpt: SplashDecodeJpeg() allocates bitmap storage using stride * height as a signed int expression. SAFE_TO_ALLOC checks an unsigned 32-bit bound, so it can accept a mathematical product above INT_MAX. The allocation expression then has signed overflow and undefined behavior. If bitmap allocation fails, the function frees splash->frames but leaves its pointer and frameCount unchanged. The buffer-allocation failure path has the same ownership problem. A subsequent SplashCleanup(), including cleanup after an unsuccessful startup splash decode, can read freed frame storage and attempt to free it again.

pulls.title: 8394923: RISC-V: Use slli+bgez for the ZGC load barrier
pulls.author: yadongw
pulls.body_excerpt: Problem The strong-reference ZGC load barrier on RISC-V tests the pointer color against the load-bad mask with li16u+andr+beqz: four instructions, two of which materialize the mask constant. The mask contains three bits in positions 12–15 and cannot fit in andi's 12-bit immediate. Solution Store the complement of the remap bits in colored pointers, following the AArch64 encoding. This makes the load-bad mask a single bit, allowing the strong-reference check in C1 and C2 to use two instructions: ``` slli tmp, ref, shift bgez tmp, good ``` The shift amount is patched to 63 - log2(load_bad_mask)

This replacement changes the uncommon_trap logic: once execution hits a trap, the VM performs deoptimization but does not recompile the method anymore.
